label: prop:isospin-singlet-binds-more
title: $\mu_- < \mu_+$ for every $q>0$ at $z = q^3/(q^2+1)$: the isospin singlet is always the more strongly bound channel
html:
Let z = q^{3}/(q^{2}+1) be the Markov parameter and let

  \mu_+ \;=\; \frac{z + q^{-1}}{q + q^{-1}},
  \qquad
  \mu_- \;=\; \frac{q - z}{q + q^{-1}}

be the interface scalars of the isospin triplet and singlet. Then

  \boxed{\;\; \mu_- \;<\; \mu_+ \qquad \text{for every } q > 0. \;\;}

The ordering is forced, not fitted

The difference of the two scalars is

  \mu_+ - \mu_- \;=\; \frac{2z - h}{q + q^{-1}},
  \qquad h = q - q^{-1},

and at z = q^{3}/(q^{2}+1) the numerator is an identity with a manifestly positive value:

  2z - h \;=\; \frac{q^{4}+1}{q\,(q^{2}+1)} .

Every factor on the right is a sum of even powers of q divided by a product of positive terms, so the sign requires no numerical input and no estimate. The denominator q + q^{-1} is positive for q > 0 by the same reading. The ordering therefore holds for the whole positive axis, not on a window around the substrate parameter.

How this ordering is read against the measured two-nucleon channels, with the values at q_0, is recorded in the two-nucleon reading.
